answer:
Neither of the two options as you have framed them. A plain containment link will not do the job, but the correction is not "model each administrative unit as its own place with a bounded period" — a CRM place cannot have a bounded period. The hundred and the rural district are instances of E4 Period; their territories are instances of E53 Place obtained by projection; and the mill's changing membership is carried by instances of E93 Presence.

1) Why plain containment fails. P89 falls within is declared E53 -> E53, so it does not attach to the mill at all. A physical thing reaches a place through P156 occupies (whose full path runs E18 P196 defines, E92, P161 has spatial projection, E53) or P53 has former or current location; so even the "plain" version would have to be a link between the mill's extent and the unit's extent. And P89 is timeless, transitive and reflexive: its scope note says it "addresses spatial containment only and does not imply any relationship between things or phenomena occupying these places". Asserting both containments would say that each spatial inclusion held at some time, never which held when, and would say nothing at all about administrative belonging. The SIG's accepted text on temporal validity (Issue 204, closed Amersfoort 2012) states the general rule: "Stating instances of such properties for an item in terms of the CRM only means that these properties existed at some time-span", and if more temporal detail is needed the events must be described explicitly.

2) Your premise about the hundred is right in its conclusion but not in its reasoning. E53 Place comprises extents in space "independent from temporal phenomena and matter"; places have no beginning or end, so the 1894 abolition cannot be an event in the life of a place. What ended in 1894 was the geopolitical unit. The CRM puts geopolitical units in E4 Period. The E4 scope note (the wording added under SIG Issue 312 'Mapping Geopolitical Units to Period', closed 2018) reads "A geopolitical unit as a specific case of an instance of E4 Period is the set of activities and phenomena related to the claim of power", names "administrative areas of countries such as districts" as its modern example, and adds "The spatiotemporal properties of Geopolitical units can be modelled through the properties inherited from E92 Spacetime Volume". Martin Doerr says the same twice on the list: in t1090, "a geopolitical entity is indeed regarded as a case (type, specialization) of E4 Period"; in t1243, arguing that the corresponding E53 is only an extent-in-a-year, "It is wrong to regard the Desert as an E53".

3) The shape I would record.
• The mill: one instance of E22 Human-Made Object, unchanged throughout. Its ground: P156 occupies an E53 Place (your grid reference / polygon).
• Sedgewick Hundred: an E4 Period, P2 has type 'hundred' (E55 Type), P4 has time-span an E52 Time-Span ending 1894, P161 has spatial projection an E53 Place 'extent of Sedgewick Hundred'.
• Whitgate Rural District: an E4 Period, P2 has type 'rural district', P4 has time-span from 1894, P161 has spatial projection its own E53 Place.
• Because the hundred's ground was folded into the district, extent-of-hundred P89 falls within extent-of-district. This is the one place P89 belongs: between two extents, not between the mill and an administrative unit.
• Membership, time-sliced: Presence-1 is an E93 Presence, P195 was a presence of the mill (the CRM's declared shortcut for mill P196 defines E92, P166 was a presence of), P164 is temporally specified by an E52 Time-Span covering the eighteenth-century estate-map period to 1894, and P10 falls within Sedgewick Hundred (E4). Presence-2 likewise from 1894, P10 falls within Whitgate Rural District.

P10 is the correct property because both ends are instances of E92 (E93 is a subclass of E92; so is E4), and the specification distinguishes it from exactly the mistake the plain-containment option would make: "It should not be confused with inclusion in the spatial and temporal projection, which may be larger", illustrated by "in 14 AD, Mesopotamia was not within the Roman Empire". Linking the mill's extent by P89 to the all-time projections of both units reproduces the Mesopotamia error — both statements are true and both are useless. The narrative section on spatiotemporal relations says of instances of E93 that "They are the basic construct to describe exactly where something was or happened at a particular time".

If your HER holds only polygons and you do not want to commit to the phenomenal extent of the unit, use the weaker P167 was within from each Presence to the E53 extent instead of P10. P167 is itself declared as a shortcut of P161 has spatial projection followed by P89 falls within — that is the "fuller chain" you anticipated, now anchored to a time-span by P164 rather than floating free.

4) Nothing here touches the mill physically. An E93 Presence is a spacetime volume, not the thing; P196/P195 relate the mill to its own trajectory through spacetime. No instance of E11 Modification, E81 Transformation or E6 Destruction is created, so the record never implies the boundary change or the renaming altered the structure.

5) The name change. P1 is identified by is deliberately time-neutral: "The property does not reveal anything about when, where and by whom this identifier was used. A more detailed representation can be made using the fully developed (i.e. indirect) path through E15 Identifier Assignment." So keep both names on the single E22 as two instances of E41 Appellation via P1 (coarse, monotonic, always true), and where the dates matter add one E15 Identifier Assignment per name: P140 assigned attribute to the mill, P141 assigned the appellation, P177 assigned property of type = P1 is identified by (E55), P4 has time-span (the estate-map period; from the 1850s censuses), P14 carried out by the estate or the enumerating authority where known. If your HER treats the two strings as its own identifiers rather than as vernacular names, the E42 Identifier variant with P37 assigned and P38 deassigned is the path the CRM actually declares behind P1 and records the supersession directly. P139 has alternative form between the two appellations is available but is equally timeless.

6) The CRM will not give you 'Hundred' or 'Rural District' classes — enumerating concrete cases is what the Minimality principle forbids. They are instances of E55 Type carried on the E4 Periods by P2 has type, which is also what lets your HER query by unit kind.

So: yes, the fact that the hundred stopped existing does force the fuller chain, but the reason is not that a place ended. It is that administrative membership is a spatiotemporal relation between a thing's presence and a phenomenon that has a lifetime, and the CRM has one construct for that — E93 Presence with P164 and P10 — while P89 has, by its own scope note, no temporal content and no bearing on the things occupying the places it relates.

rejected_alternatives.option: E53 Place for Sedgewick Hundred and Whitgate Rural District, joined by P89 falls within
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E53 comprises extents in space 'independent from temporal phenomena and matter', so a place cannot be abolished in 1894; and P89 is timeless, transitive and reflexive and 'addresses spatial containment only and does not imply any relationship between things or phenomena occupying these places'. Doerr in t1243 rules that only 'Extent of X in year Y' is an E53, not the named unit itself.

rejected_alternatives.option: A subclass of E7 Activity for the administrative unit
rejected_alternatives.why_not: This was Richard Light's own first proposal in t1093 ('Administrative units have a temporal dimension, so should be a subclass of E7_Activity'). Doerr rejected it there: 'not all things having a temporal dimension are activities'. The SIG settled the question the other way under Issue 312, placing geopolitical units in E4 Period.

rejected_alternatives.option: E74 Group (or E40 Legal Body) for the hundred
rejected_alternatives.why_not: That models the body that administered the area, not the area's jurisdictional extent; the case needs the mill's membership of a territory, which a Group has no spatial projection to supply. Light raised and dismissed this himself in t1093: 'It's not a place (certainly not as defined in E53_Place); nor is it an E74_Group'.

rejected_alternatives.option: A bare E92 Spacetime Volume for each administrative unit
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E92 alone drops the phenomenal identity of the unit and the properties that carry it: P4 has time-span, P9 consists of, P7 took place at. E4 Period is the declared specialization for geopolitical units and inherits everything E92 offers anyway, per the E4 scope note.

rejected_alternatives.option: E9 Move to record the 1894 change of administrative area
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E9 comprises changes of the physical location of an E19 Physical Object. The mill did not move; the administrative geography moved around it. Using E9 would assert precisely the physical change the record must avoid implying.

rejected_alternatives.option: E11 Modification or E81 Transformation for either change
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Nothing was created, altered or destroyed. Both the renaming and the boundary reform leave the E22 numerically and physically identical, which is why the whole answer keeps them off the physical thing and on a Presence and an Identifier Assignment.

E27 comprises pieces of land or sea floor. The site is a legitimate separate entity for an HER, but it is not the structure that was renamed, so it cannot carry the appellation history; and adding it here would not change the administrative-membership answer at all.

rejected_alternatives.option: F52 Name Use Activity / R64 used name (FRBRoo)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: It surfaced as the FRBRoo route to dated naming (t0821), but the index carries no scope note for it here and it is a bibliographic-domain class. CRMbase already declares E15 Identifier Assignment as the fully developed path behind P1, so no extension is needed.

siblings_considered.why_not: E25 Human-Made Feature covers features purposely created but physically inseparable from a larger thing - scratches, artificial caves, water channels. A windmill is a free-standing structure with boundaries that separate it objectively from other objects, which is E22's own criterion. If your HER treats the mill as inseparable from its mound or site, E25 would be the right pick instead, and nothing else in this answer changes.

E73 Information Object is the other subclass of E90 and would be the estate map or the census return - an identifiable immaterial item with propositional content. 'Fen End Mill' is a sign used by convention to refer to the mill, not a documented information unit, so E41 is the class and E73 is the source that evidences it.

E17 Type Assignment is the sibling a reader would raise, since both date an act of ascription. But E17 assigns an E55 Type, and E55's scope note draws the line explicitly: types 'represent concepts, in contrast to instances of E41 Appellation which are used to name instances'. 'Bell's Mill' names the mill, it does not classify it. E17 is however the right class for typing the unit as 'hundred' if you want that ascription dated too.

E93 Presence is the other subclass of E92 and is a time-slice whose temporal extent is chosen by the researcher in order to find a spatial extent. Sedgewick Hundred is not a slice of anything: it is the phenomenon itself, with its own beginning and end, and it is what the E93 slices are measured against. I do use E93, but for the mill's whereabouts, not for the unit.

E2 Temporal Entity is the sibling under E1 that tempts you to record '1700-1894' as a phenomenon. It should not be: the phenomenon is already the E4 Period (itself an E2), and an extra E2 for the same stretch would duplicate the unit. E52 carries no semantic connotations about what happened in it, which is exactly what P164 and P4 need.

E92 Spacetime Volume is the sibling under E1 and is where the time already lives, on the E4 Periods. The extent your HER holds as a polygon is a purely spatial projection with no time in it, and P161's range, P167's range and P89's domain and range are all E53. Substituting E92 would re-import a temporal dimension the projection does not have.

E4 Period is the only other subclass of E92. The mill's whereabouts between the 1700s and 1894 is not a set of coherent phenomena identified by social or physical coherence; it is a slice of the mill's trajectory cut at a time-span I chose, which is E93's definition word for word. Making it an E4 would also wrongly make the mill's location a historical period in its own right.

E90 Symbolic Object is the sibling under E28 and is where the strings live - it is the parent of E41, which I use for the two mill names. 'Hundred' and 'rural district' are concepts from a controlled vocabulary used to characterise the E4 Periods, not the symbols denoting them, so they belong in E55.

notes:
Two things the tools made harder than they needed to be. First, 'docs' truncates each hit to roughly 300 characters, so the narrative passages that carry the actual reasoning (crm732#s0084 and crm732#s0085) could only be read in full by going through --json; there is no way to page a chunk. Second, the episode summaries attached to 'concept' output are unreliable: the entry dated 2017-08-25 under both E53 and E93, labelled 'Modeling populated places with temporal and spatial variation using sp', points at t1019, which is entirely a discussion of E30 Right and end-of-existence for rights. I lost a read on that. The thread pointers themselves were good: t1090, t1093 and t1243 between them gave the SIG's position verbatim, and 'issues' found Issue 312, which is the decision that put the geopolitical-unit wording into the E4 scope note.

One open point I could not settle from the tools: whether a windmill should be E22 Human-Made Object or E25 Human-Made Feature. The reference document's examples for both classes (a locomotive, the Rosetta Stone; a ship canal, a nose) do not include buildings, and searching the list found only relabelling debates (t1081, t1194) and one 2025 remark that an E22 can become an E25 when incorporated into a larger object (t1874). I chose E22 and flagged the alternative rather than assert a rule I could not find. Nothing else in the answer depends on that choice.
